subject: Mid-trial scope surge and updated acceptance rubric
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Shah <priya@orchardai.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: Post-demo recap + proposed mid-trial plan changes

Hi Priya — thanks again for a great session this morning. Quick recap and a proposal so we have clear next steps going into the midpoint of the trial.

Call highlights:
- Orchard wants us to validate two additional workloads mid-trial: (1) order-reconciliation (matching support tickets to orders) and (2) cart-summary generation (short human-readable cart summaries for support agents).
- Current acceptance criteria are focused on F1/overall relevance on the chat flows; customer asked for per-intent precision/recall thresholds and a small-scale business-rule accuracy check for order reconciliation.
- You can provide a 7-day sample of anonymized order/support pairs and a spreadsheet of rules you currently apply.

Proposed changes (summary):
1) Add the two workloads above to the trial scope as optional "surge" test cases. We will treat them as gated; the baseline chat flows remain primary.
2) Update acceptance rubric to include: precision@10 >= 85% for cart-summary (human eval), order-reconciliation exact-match >= 92% on the business-rule dataset, and end-to-end latency median < 300ms on the high-throughput endpoint.
3) Timeline: extend the trial midpoint evaluation window by 14 days to accommodate data prep + two evaluation sweeps. New checkpoint: Dec 15 technical review -> final acceptance Dec 22.
4) Ownership: Redwood will own instrumentation and eval scripts (Rishi); Marissa will own acceptance rubric and reporting; Marcus (me) will coordinate commercial approvals and any contract amendment.

Attachments: POC-Acceptance-Rubric-v1.xlsx (initial rubric draft).

Next actions I propose:
- Priya: confirm you can share the 7-day anonymized sample and the business-rule spreadsheet by EOD Dec 3.
- Redwood (Rishi): prepare a preliminary eval plan and QA checklist by Dec 6.
- Marissa: draft an updated acceptance rubric (v2) if needed after we ingest the sample.

If that works, I’ll update the HubSpot deal notes and draft a short amendment for the trial timeline so procurement/legal can review. Happy to jump on a 30-min sync if you prefer to walk through the rubric.

Thanks,
Marcus
Marcus Lin
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0192

From: Priya Shah <priya@orchardai.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Amit Rao <amit@orchardai.com>, legal@orchardai.com
Date: Thu, 03 Dec 2026 11:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap + proposed mid-trial plan changes

Thanks Marcus — yes, the call was useful. Quick responses inline.

- We can share an anonymized 7-day window of order + support ticket pairs. I’ll have Amit prep the extract and share a CSV by EOD Dec 4. Attached is a small sample (sample_orders.csv) pulled from staging — note fields are redacted.
- Procurement/legal will need to see the timeline amendment and a short note on data retention/retention controls (we keep data for 30 days in staging). Please include the retention window in the amendment.
- On acceptance: 92% exact-match for order-reconciliation seems aggressive. Can we consider a two-tier check: (a) business-rule pass-rate >= 90% for machine-assisted reconciliation (where agents review suggested matches) and (b) a separate automation-only benchmark target if we hit it? That gives us a path to success if we choose to accept machine-assisted results.

Also — cost: if the trial is extended 14 days and we add the surge workloads, will there be incremental charges? We need an estimate to confirm with Procurement.

Amit/Legal: looped in for visibility; Amit will upload the sample CSV shortly.

Thanks,
Priya
Interim Head of Product — Orchard AI
priya@orchardai.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Shah <priya@orchardai.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 06 Dec 2026 08:22:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap + proposed mid-trial plan changes

Hi Priya — looping in details on acceptance and instrumentation. Thanks for the sample CSV, Amit — that helped.

Proposal from the Redwood side (concrete):
- Acceptance rubric v2 (attached) will have two tracks for order-reconciliation: 
  * Machine-assisted acceptance: business-rule pass-rate >= 90% when suggestions are shown to agents (we measure agent-acceptance rate on a 1,000-sample blind set).
  * Automation-only acceptance: exact-match >= 92% on a holdout set (only used if Orchard opts into full automation).
- For cart-summary, we will run human raters on a 500-sample set and report precision@10 and average helpfulness score (1-5). Target: precision@10 >= 85 and helpfulness >= 3.8.
- Instrumentation: Rishi will deploy a temporary logging endpoint (no PII captured, hashes only) to capture match-scores and latency for the surge tests. Logging retention will be limited to 30 days to match your policy; we will include that language in the amendment.
- Cost: There will be a modest trial surcharge to cover the extra eval sweeps and additional routing capacity for the surge workloads. Marcus — can you provide a ballpark estimate for procurement? I’d suggest we offer the customer a capped surcharge (e.g., $3k) and absorb any overage beyond that for this trial.

Action items and owners:
- Amit (Orchard): provide complete 7-day extract + business-rule spreadsheet (Due: Dec 4) — done, sample received.
- Rishi (Redwood): instrument logging endpoint and evaluation harness (Due: Dec 10).
- Marissa (Redwood): finalize acceptance-rubric-v2 and share (Due: Dec 9).
- Marcus (Redwood): draft amendment wording and estimated surcharge for Procurement (Due: Dec 8).

Attachment: POC-Acceptance-Rubric-v2.xlsx.

If Orchard agrees to the two-track acceptance for reconciliation, we can move forward without pushing the automation-only target immediately. That should keep momentum while giving a clear path to higher automation.

Best,
Marissa
Senior Customer Success Manager — Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai

Date: Tue, 15 Dec 2026 16:42:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap + proposed mid-trial plan changes — confirmed scope & next steps

Priya — thanks for the prompt reviews and for sharing the data. Quick update and confirmation of next steps so procurement/legal have what they need.

What’s agreed:
- Scope: add the two surge workloads (order-reconciliation and cart-summary) as a gated mid-trial expansion. We will run two evaluation sweeps during the extended window.
- Acceptance rubric: we’ll proceed with the two-track approach for reconciliation (machine-assisted primary track, automation-only as optional). Cart-summary targets as in v2.
- Timeline: extended evaluation window; technical checkpoint Dec 15 (today) and final acceptance checkpoint Dec 22.
- Data & retention: Redwood will only ingest hashed identifiers and will retain logs for 30 days; we will include a paragraph in the amendment describing controls and deletion timeline.
- Cost: Redwood proposes a capped surcharge of $3,000 for the additional eval runs and surge capacity; we will absorb any overages beyond the cap for this trial. Marcus to follow up with a short amendment and DocuSign link.

Related links: HubSpot deal (see link), Drive folder with rubric and sample; I’ve also initiated a DocuSign amendment template — will send the link by EOD.

Next meetings:
- Dec 17 @ 10am PT: 30-min technical sync (Rishi + Amit + Orchard infra).
- Dec 22 @ 11am PT: final acceptance review (stakeholders + Redwood ops).

If legal wants changes to the retention paragraph we’ll iterate quickly — Marissa, loop in legal if needed.

Thanks all — looking forward to closing the trial strong.

Marcus
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.ai
